title: Money and how we use it

sub.en: Look at the pairs. Which one names a finished time, and which one runs up to now?

items.q: I ___ this account for ten years. (I still have it)
items.why: A situation that started in the past and is still true takes the present perfect. A finished time takes the Past Simple.

items.q: I ___ this account in 2014. (a finished time)

items.why: for + a length of time (for ten years). since + a starting point (since 2014, since I was a child).

items.q: How long ___ you had that car?
I ___ two thousand from my brother last July.

tts: I’ve got some things here that I don’t think we really need. Maybe we could get rid of them? — Like what?
Well, like this Japanese knife that you bought. It takes up so much space in the drawer and it’s not very useful. — Not very useful? It’s essential!
Essential for what? — For chopping vegetables! — How often do you chop vegetables with it? — …
Exactly. You’ve had it for six years and you’ve used it twice.

tts: Hi, can I help you? — Yes, I hope so. I’m looking for one of those little machines. I don’t know the name, but you use it to record things.
How big is it? — Oh, it’s quite small. It fits in your hand or your pocket. It looks like a mobile phone.
Oh, yes, I know what you mean. It’s called a voice recorder.

acts.title: The drawer
text: We have lived in this flat since 2016 and in that time we have filled one drawer with objects nobody can explain.

There is a Japanese knife. My husband bought it six years ago and he has used it twice. He says it is essential. There are four phone chargers, and only one of them fits a phone we still own. There is a set of keys that opens nothing in this building; we have tried every door.

There is also a receipt from 2018 for a jacket that neither of us remembers buying. We haven’t thrown it away, because as long as we have the receipt we could theoretically get a refund, and that idea is worth more to us than the jacket ever was.
Last Sunday we agreed to empty the drawer. We took everything out, looked at it, and put it all back. It took forty minutes.

items.s: They have lived in the flat since 2016.
The husband has used the knife many times.
One of the four chargers fits a phone they own.
The keys open a door in the building.

write.q: Write about money and time: 6 sentences. Two with the present perfect and for, two with since, one with a finished past time and the Past Simple, and one about something you can’t afford.
write.model: I’ve had the same bank account for eleven years and I’ve never had a reason to change it. I’ve lived in this flat since 2019, and the rent has gone up twice since I moved in. I haven’t borrowed money from anybody since university. I borrowed two thousand from my brother in 2018 and I paid it back in the same month, which he still mentions. I can’t afford to move this year. I’m saving up, slowly.

speak.q: Answer out loud: How long have you lived where you live? How long have you had your phone? When did you last borrow money? What can’t you afford at the moment?
speak.model: I’ve lived here for four years — since 2020. I’ve had this phone for about eighteen months. I last borrowed money in 2019, from my brother. I can’t afford a car at the moment, so I’m saving up.
